# dsh-session-requirement

Per-conversation **session requirement / constraint** box for DeepSeek Harness.
It lives in the conv

ersation title row and lets you write one standing
requirement for *this* conversation, plus pick sk

ills with `@`, and have all of
it attached to every message you send.

The box is **off until you switch it on**. The switch lives in
**Settings → General → 本对话的整体要求**; fl

ip it and the box appears in the
title row immediately — no reload, no restart. Flip it back and the

box is gone,
and nothing is attached to your messages either.
Collapsed, it is one line at the right end of the title row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Focused, it lifts out of the row as a floating card — the header never grows:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Behaviour

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- || GUI switch | one toggle in Settings → General, stored globally in t

he state file; off on a fresh install |
| Show/hide | off renders nothing at all — no empty gap and

no slot in the title row; on mounts the field in every conversation at once |
| Placement | `convers
ation.session.header.utilities`, `order: 0` — the right-aligned utility area of the Session title ro

w (the `创建/标准模式` line), left of the corner controls |
| Size | a fixed 380px × 28px slot, so the tit
le row never reflows. On focus the field lifts out of flow as a 470px floating card (`position: abso

lute`) over the tab row, because the header must not grow |
| Blank conversations | the shipped head
er hides its whole title-row chrome while a conversation is still blank, so the same field also regi
sters in `conversation.input.dock` (`order: -100`) and shows there until the title row appears. A mo
dule-level seat registry keeps exactly one copy on screen; the dock copy is the full-width, in-flow

variant |
| Collapsed | one line; expands to four lines on focus; collapses on blur without losing t

ext |
| Scope | text, chips, and the per-conversation switch are stored per conversation; a new conv

ersation starts empty and off |
| Effective | `requirementText.trim().length > 0 \|\| skillIds.lengt

h > 0` |
| Switch | grey while there is no content and clicking it focuses the input; turns on by it
self on the first effective content; turning it off keeps text and skills but stops attaching them;

clearing everything greys it again |
| Attach | only when the GUI switch is on, the per-conversation

switch is on, **and** the content is effective |
| `@` picker | opens on `@` at line start or after
whitespace; filters by name, description and `whenToUse`; `↑`/`↓` move, `Enter` picks, `Esc` closes
, click picks; empty result and load failure show an inline message instead of breaking the input |
| Chips | a picked skill becomes a non-editable `@name ×` chip; `×` removes it; `Backspace` in an em

pty input removes the last one; duplicates are ignored; the cap is `maxSkills` (default 10) |

## How attachment works

`conversation.send()` on the client is a pure pass-through — there is no
outgoing-prompt transform t

o hook. The durable, model-visible seam is the host's
`agent/pre-step`; when the claimed message bat

ch contains a real user message
(a fresh send, not a tool-loop follow-up) this row appends one extra

al user message
(a fresh send, not a tool-loop follow-up) this row appends one extra
`user/message`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

It is committed through the harness's own `surfaceOp: "append"` path with
`source.kind = "session-re

quirement"`, so it lands in the transcript like the
built-in `/skill` invocation injection — it neve
r impersonates a user gesture.
## HTTP surface
| Route | Purpose |
| `GET /api/session-requirement?sessionId=…` | read one conversation's state (also reports `visible`

) |
| `GET /api/session-requirement?mode=settings` | read the GUI switch alone, with no conversation

|
| `POST /api/session-requirement` | write one conversation's state: `{ sessionId, requirementText

, requirementEnabled, skillIds }` |
| `POST /api/session-requirement` `{ visible }` | flip the GUI s

Enabled, skillIds }` |
| `POST /api/session-requirement` `{ visible }` | flip the GUI switch alone |

State lives in `<DSH_HOME>/session-requirement.json`, written atomically
(`.tmp` + rename):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Requests are rejected with `400` rather than silently corrected when `sessionId`
is malformed, the t

ext exceeds `maxTextLength`, or `skillIds` is not a
deduplicated list of at most `maxSkills` skill n

xceeds `maxTextLength`, or `skillIds` is not a
deduplicated list of at most `maxSkills` skill names.
## Command

`/requirement` prints the current conversation's state; `/requirement clear`
clears and disables it.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** (desktop or web), Cordis v4.
- No npm dependencies. The host half impor

ts only Node built-ins; the browser
half is a hand-written CJS bundle that takes `react` from the ha

built-ins; the browser
half is a hand-written CJS bundle that takes `react` from the harness loader.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Point your profile at the checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then reinstall the profile and restart DeepSeek Harness — the browser half ships
as a static client
bundle, so a page refresh alone is not enough.

> **Use `link:`, not `file:`.** pnpm copies a `file:` directory dependency and
> caches it, so later

edits never reach the profile. `link:` creates a junction
> (Windows) or symlink, so the profile al
ways reads the current source.
## Uninstall

Remove the dependency and the bundle entry, reinstall, restart. The host row
drops its route, its `a

gent/pre-step` listener, and flushes pending state on
dispose; the browser half removes its `<style

data-plugin="dsh-session-requirement">`
node, its document listeners, its debounce timers, its cache

s, and aborts
in-flight requests. Deleting `<DSH_HOME>/session-requirement.json` is optional.
## Configuration

| `maxSkills` | `10` | maximum chips per conversation |
| `maxTextLength` | `8000` | maximum require
